Week 10: review the exercises and assemble the folio
Weeks 11 to 12: introduce the drawing project, research, set personal project aims

Weeks 18 to 21: finish assessment and feedback

Task 2: a drawing project judged against a checklist of components and overall outcome, with written feedback, due week 18

syllabi.notes: 80 nominal hours over a 21-week term, so 3.8 hours per week is my division, not a stated contact figure. This is the Term 2 2021 Brunswick offering; the current timetable may differ. Closest Melbourne evidence of how a vocational drawing unit is paced: eight weeks of exercises, then a long self-directed project.

sequence: A run of projects drawing manufactured and natural forms, including the human figure

Use of line, tone, shape, movement and texture

sequence: Week 1: blind, semi-blind and continuous contour, gesture, circles and ellipses
Week 2: sighting and alignment to judge proportion
Week 3: negative space, first look at value
Week 4: more value work, subtractive drawing, light and shadow for form
Week 5: one-point and two-point perspective
Week 6: pen techniques (hatching, cross-hatching, stippling, scumbling)
Week 7: portraits and face proportions
Week 8: landscape, with outdoor sessions if the weather allows
assessment_criteria: No grading or assessment criteria stated; this is a non-credit class

sequence: Weeks 1 to 2: charcoal and pencil handling, pictorial space, edges, proportion exercises
Weeks 3 to 4: composition frameworks, positive and negative space, shape, intro to contour line
Weeks 5 to 6: cross-contour, broken line, line weight to build volume
Week 7: blind contour, continuous line, mass gesture
Week 8: one- and two-point perspective
Week 9: ellipses, foreshortening, inclined planes
Weeks 10 to 12: midterm check-ins, then value range, shadow, contrast, blending, chiaroscuro
Week 15: wet media (ink) and tonal structure
Weeks 16 to 17: head and facial planes, portraits, figure analysis, pattern and texture
Weeks 17 to 18: final drawing and critique
assessment_criteria: Class work, including taking part in discussions and critiques: 75 percent
Homework across the whole term: 25 percent
Late work marked down a full grade

Competent handling of materials

The programme page https://www.florenceacademyofart.com/certificate-programs/foundation-in-graphic-art/ describes the same three stages (foundations, figure and portrait, landscape).

consensus_sequence.name: Marks, line and gesture
consensus_sequence.common_benchmark: Draws a household object in confident, mostly unbroken lines with at least three line weights, and captures the direction and weight of a short pose in under a minute.

consensus_sequence.name: Measuring and shape
topics: Proportion and placement on the page
consensus_sequence.common_benchmark: Draws a three-object still life from observation whose proportions and spacing hold up when laid over the reference.

consensus_sequence.name: Perspective and construction
consensus_sequence.common_benchmark: Builds boxes, cylinders and a simple interior with one consistent horizon and vanishing points, without a ruler for the ellipses.

consensus_sequence.name: Value and form
consensus_sequence.common_benchmark: Renders a sphere, cube or egg under one light with a readable light side, core shadow, reflected light and cast shadow.

consensus_sequence.name: Surface, texture and media
topics: Pen, ink and other wet media
consensus_sequence.common_benchmark: Makes cloth, wood, metal and skin look different from each other using only mark and tone.

consensus_sequence.name: Head, portrait and figure
topics: Portrait from a model or photo
consensus_sequence.common_benchmark: Draws a head or figure in about 20 minutes with believable proportions and a clear light pattern.

consensus_sequence.name: Space, landscape and a finished piece
topics: Space in a still life or interior
consensus_sequence.common_benchmark: Completes one longer, composed drawing of a self-chosen subject and can explain what works and what does not.

consensus_sequence.name: Ideas, sketchbook and invention
topics: A self-directed series or project with critique
consensus_sequence.common_benchmark: Develops one idea through a page of thumbnails, picks the strongest, and finishes it as a project with feedback.

benchmarks.check: One 60-minute sitting: ten 1-minute gestures from a timed pose source; a 10-minute continuous-line drawing of one household object, looking mostly at the object; a 15-minute drawing of the same object from the other side using at least three line weights. Next day, draw it again from memory in 3 minutes and compare.
pass_signs: Lines are drawn from the shoulder or elbow and committed, not scratchy repeated strokes
At least three distinct line weights are visible and used on purpose
Gestures show the pose's main direction before any detail
The memory sketch gets the overall shape and placement roughly right
Your log shows regular sessions over the last six weeks (a record, not a streak)

benchmarks.check: From imagination, draw a cube, a cylinder and a sphere standing on a tiled floor in two-point perspective, then a street corner with three buildings, then one invented object (a kettle, a lamp) built from boxes and cylinders from three different viewpoints. About 90 minutes total.
pass_signs: Extend the receding lines with a ruler: they meet within about a thumb-width of one vanishing point per set
One horizon line serves the whole page
Ellipse minor axes sit square to the cylinder's axis, and ellipses get rounder the further they sit from the horizon line
Objects get smaller and overlap correctly with distance
The invented object reads as the same thing from all three viewpoints

benchmarks.check: Draw a three-object still life from a reference photo in 25 minutes using sighting and negative space only (no grid, no tracing). Scale the photo to the drawing's size and overlay it at 50 percent opacity in Krita or on tracing paper. Repeat with a second subject a week later and compare the two overlays.
pass_signs: Key landmark points land within about 5 percent of the image height from the photo's positions
Each object's height-to-width ratio is within about 10 percent
The shapes between and around objects match the photo
The second overlay is closer than the first
When the drawing is flipped horizontally, you can spot your own errors before overlaying

benchmarks.check: Under one lamp, draw a sphere or egg, a cube and a cup with a 5-step value scale beside them (45 minutes). Then render one glossy object (a steel spoon) and one matte object (a lemon or an eraser) in 60 minutes.
pass_signs: Light direction is the same on every object and the cast shadows agree with it
Light, halftone, core shadow, reflected light and cast shadow are each separate and readable
Photographed and posterised to four grey levels, the drawing breaks into the same big shapes as the real set-up
Darkest darks and lightest lights are not used until the end
A viewer can tell glossy from matte without being told

benchmarks.check: From timed reference: three 30-second gestures, one 5-minute and one 20-minute figure, then a 30-minute three-quarter head built from a simple skull block. Finish with a mannequin figure in a pose of your choice drawn from three viewpoints.
pass_signs: The gesture line shows weight and action; the shoulders and hips tilt against each other
Limb lengths and head count agree with the reference to within about half a head
On the head, the eye line sits near the middle of the skull, and nose, mouth and ear line up with the right guide lines
Planes of the face read under a simple light direction
The mannequin keeps the same proportions in all three views

benchmarks.check: Three 45-minute studies from photos or life: a branch with leaves (growth pattern and overlap), an animal built from simple volumes, and a building facade or street scene. Add one page of four material swatches (wood, metal, glass, fabric).
pass_signs: A stranger names each subject without a label
The plant shows how leaves attach and overlap, not a row of symbols
The animal's landmarks (joints, ribcage, head) sit in believable positions
The building keeps consistent perspective and a believable rhythm of windows and doors against human scale
The four materials are distinct from mark and value alone

benchmarks.check: From a one-line brief (for example, a tired lighthouse keeper in a storm), make nine 2-inch value thumbnails for composition, choose one, then draw a front, side and back view of the character and a six-expression sheet.
pass_signs: The thumbnails use different layouts and each has a clear focal point
The chosen silhouette still reads at thumbnail size
Guide lines across the three views line up on head, shoulder, hip and knee landmarks
All six expressions read without captions
You can state in one sentence what the picture is about

benchmarks.check: Make a 2-hour colour study from a photo or a CC0 museum painting using 4 to 6 colours: first a grey value underpainting, then colour on top. Repeat it digitally in Krita with named layers, and export a PNG at a size you set in advance.
pass_signs: Converted to greyscale, the colour version keeps the value structure of the underpainting
The palette is limited and holds together; shadows and lights follow one temperature logic
Edges vary between hard and soft on purpose
The digital file has clean, named layers and exports without surprises
The result is close enough to the source that a side-by-side check shows the same light and mood

practice_library.title: Line of Action
practice_library.free_notes: The owner states the original practice tools stay free for everyone, with banner ads for free users. Paid membership (USD, monthly): Doodler $1.49 removes ads and adds review, goal tracking and 5 critique uploads a month; Apprentice $4.99 adds personal photos and 20 uploads; Master $14.95 adds unlimited uploads and 3,000+ extra figure images. 33 percent student or teacher discount. The membership page does not list limits for free accounts.
practice_library.licence: Images belong to their photographers; no reuse licence is given. Use for private practice only.
practice_library.notes: Figure, animals, faces and expressions, hands and feet, scenes and environments, 360-degree views. Some figure reference is nude. Membership details: https://line-of-action.com/membership

practice_library.title: Quickposes
practice_library.free_notes: Timed practice with a time limit you choose, 20-image challenges, and untimed random poses are available without paying per the page. Optional extras: tips of 3, 5 or 10 euros and a desktop app at 15 euros. No subscription is listed.
practice_library.licence: Not stated on the page; treat the images as practice reference only.
practice_library.notes: Page does not say what an account unlocks.

practice_library.title: SketchDaily Reference
practice_library.free_notes: Described as free by two secondary pages (a Proko community thread and a pose-site roundup). The home page itself is a script-driven app and returned only its title to my fetch, so I could not read pricing on the provider's own page.
practice_library.licence: No licence stated (per the roundup, which advises practice use and no commercial use of work made from it).
practice_library.notes: Per the Proko thread: stationary or action poses, other subject categories, a class mode, and uploading your own photos. Free status comes from secondary sources only.

practice_library.title: Posemaniacs
practice_library.free_notes: Home page calls its 3D pose references royalty free and offers figure, muscle and face references plus a pose library. It does not state pricing, and the site also lists video courses and seminars that may be paid.
practice_library.licence: Pose references described as royalty free; the Terms of use page was not read.
practice_library.notes: Free status is not confirmed on the page text I could read; check the Terms of use link before relying on it.

practice_library.title: Magic Poser (free tier)
practice_library.free_notes: Free forever: one model per scene with unlimited props, all 3D editor features, body, hand and foot posing, one directional light, 50 preset poses, 10 props, 2D image export, unlimited local saves. Not free: body morphs, 3D import and export, more than one model, spot and point lights. Pro is $9.99 one-time (600+ poses, morphs, more characters); Master is $14.99 per month (3,000+ poses, 3D export). Both have a 7-day trial.
practice_library.licence: Your own renders; the site's terms were not read.
practice_library.notes: One model is enough for pose, perspective and lighting studies. Use the 2D export as reference for your own drawing.

practice_library.title: AdorkaStock
practice_library.free_notes: A free pose gallery and a timed Sketch tool are listed; the page does not say whether Sketch is free. Paid extras: themed packs on Ko-fi, a Patreon with critiques and 360 videos, and a pose book. Prices are not shown.
practice_library.licence: Free images are released under a Creative Commons licence, covering personal and professional art use per the page; the exact CC variant is not named and there is a separate User License and Terms page. The page asks for no AI use (noai metadata).
practice_library.notes: Character reference sheets and sitting or group poses are mostly in the paid packs.

practice_library.title: PoseMyArt
practice_library.free_notes: A pose-site roundup describes it as a rotatable 3D pose library usable for commercial work, with credit appreciated and no paid tier mentioned. The site blocked my fetch (robots), so this is secondary evidence only.
practice_library.licence: Per the roundup: commercial use allowed, credit appreciated. Not confirmed on the provider's page.
practice_library.notes: Listed so the report writer can check it; do not publish as free until confirmed.

practice_library.title: JookpubStock
practice_library.free_notes: The home page labels its reference photos free and sorts them into full body, close ups (portrait, hands, feet), props, clothing, and stock (animals, nature, objects, textures). It links to Patreon, Ko-fi and VGen shops without saying what they cost.
practice_library.licence: Licence is not stated on the home page. A pose-site roundup says personal and commercial use is allowed except for NFTs or AI; check the Rules and Terms pages.
practice_library.notes: Useful for hands, feet and props as well as full figures.

practice_library.title: Pexels
practice_library.free_notes: Photos and videos are free to download and use.
practice_library.licence: Pexels License: use and modify freely; attribution not required; you may not sell unaltered copies, imply endorsement, or put identifiable people in an offensive light.
practice_library.notes: Search by subject and lighting (for example, 'hard light still life') to get value-study reference.

practice_library.title: Unsplash
practice_library.free_notes: Images are free to download, copy, modify and use, including commercially.
practice_library.licence: Unsplash License: no permission needed; attribution not required; you cannot compile the images into a competing service.
practice_library.notes: Good for architecture and landscape reference.

practice_library.title: Pixabay
practice_library.free_notes: Content is free to use and modify.
practice_library.licence: Pixabay Content License summary: no attribution needed; no selling unchanged copies; no commercial use showing identifiable brands; only the full licence text is binding.
practice_library.notes: The same library mixes photos, illustrations and vectors, so filter to photos for observation work.

practice_library.title: StockSnap
practice_library.free_notes: Photos are free to download, edit and use.
practice_library.licence: CC0. Attribution not required; you may not imply the photographer or anyone shown endorses a product.

practice_library.title: Burst
practice_library.free_notes: Described on the page as a free stock photo platform; photos are free for personal and commercial use with no attribution required.
practice_library.licence: Burst licence; the full licence page was not read.
practice_library.notes: Redirects from burst.shopify.com to this address.

practice_library.title: Wikimedia Commons
practice_library.free_notes: Page states about 50.7 million freely usable media files that anyone can contribute to.
practice_library.licence: Each file carries its own licence (public domain, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA and others); read the licence box on the file page before reusing it. I could not open the reuse guidance page.
practice_library.notes: Strong for anatomy plates, architecture, plants, animals and public-domain illustration.

practice_library.title: Rawpixel Public Domain
practice_library.free_notes: The page calls the collection free to use under CC0 and says it draws on its own originals and museum works, enhanced digitally. It links Pricing and Licenses pages that I did not read, and download limits are not stated.
practice_library.licence: CC0 as stated on the page; check each item.
practice_library.notes: Enhanced scans of museum art are handy for colour and composition studies. Premium content exists elsewhere on the site.

practice_library.title: Flickr Commons
practice_library.free_notes: A programme that gives public access to photo archives from over 100 member institutions, starting with the Library of Congress in 2008.
practice_library.licence: Rights wording differs by institution; the page I read did not explain the rights statement.
practice_library.notes: Old photographs of people, places and objects with no modern styling.

practice_library.title: Library of Congress Free to Use and Reuse
practice_library.free_notes: More than 100 themed sets of rights-free images, each about 25 to 50 items.
practice_library.licence: The page calls the sets free to use and reuse; the page metadata says only the site text is a US government work. Check each item's rights note.
practice_library.notes: Sets worth trying: Dragons, Birds, Horses, Athletes, Japanese Fine Prints, Art of the Book.

practice_library.title: Biodiversity Heritage Library
practice_library.provider: Biodiversity Heritage Library (Smithsonian Libraries and Archives hosts)
practice_library.free_notes: Free access to scanned biodiversity books and journals.
practice_library.licence: Image rights are set per item; the home page does not state them. The site notes intermittent PDF problems and an uncertain funding future.
practice_library.notes: Old natural-history plates are a good source for animal and plant structure and for creature design ideas.

practice_library.title: Morguefile
practice_library.free_notes: Page title says free photographs for commercial use; I could not read terms from the page text.
practice_library.licence: Morguefile licence; not read.
practice_library.notes: Unverified: the fetched page returned only a title.

practice_library.title: The Met Open Access
practice_library.free_notes: Over 492,000 images of public-domain works are free to download; look for the OA icon. A CSV dataset and a JSON API with high-resolution JPEGs are available.
practice_library.licence: CC0.
practice_library.notes: Search the drawings and prints holdings for master copies and the Open Access filter in the online collection.

practice_library.title: Rijksmuseum image reuse policy
practice_library.free_notes: Many images are public domain or CC0 and usable commercially without asking; credit is requested.
practice_library.licence: Public domain or CC0 where the museum holds no rights; CC BY 4.0 where copyright applies; some images are restricted and marked on the collection site.
practice_library.notes: Policy page only. I could not confirm a Rijksstudio download page, so find downloads through the museum's collection site.

practice_library.title: National Gallery of Art Open Access Images
practice_library.free_notes: More than 60,000 images can be downloaded from object pages; the museum says they are free for any use, commercial or not. The data set (not the images) is CC0 on GitHub.
practice_library.licence: Dataset CC0; the page does not name a licence for the images themselves beyond free for any use.
practice_library.notes: Filtered search for downloadable works: nga.gov/artwork-search?download=1

practice_library.title: Art Institute of Chicago Public Domain Images
practice_library.free_notes: Over 50,000 public-domain images, downloadable from the artwork page; no download button means the work is not public domain. IIIF manifests are provided.
practice_library.licence: CC0. The museum asks for a caption: artist, title, date, The Art Institute of Chicago.
practice_library.notes: Tick the public domain box in the advanced filter.

practice_library.title: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access
practice_library.free_notes: High-resolution images of more than half the collection are free; a no-key API covers 61,000+ records; data is on GitHub, Internet Archive and Wikimedia Commons.
practice_library.licence: CC0.
practice_library.notes: 3D scans of some objects are viewable on Sketchfab, which is handy for lighting studies.

practice_library.title: NGV Collection Online (public-domain downloads)
practice_library.free_notes: Over 30,000 high-resolution images of public-domain works can be downloaded by clicking the download icon. The page says downloads are free for non-commercial use and publications.
practice_library.licence: NGV terms (non-commercial), not a Creative Commons licence; see the NGV reproductions page for detail.
practice_library.notes: Local Melbourne option. The page asks users to flag culturally sensitive First Nations material through its form.

practice_library.title: Smithsonian Open Access
practice_library.free_notes: More than 5.2 million 2D and 3D digital items; a filtered link opens the CC0 media search. Developer API available.
practice_library.licence: CC0 for items marked open access.
practice_library.notes: Strong for natural history, tools and everyday objects.

practice_library.title: Getty Open Content Program
practice_library.free_notes: Over 160,000 images (86,000+ Getty Museum, 78,000+ Getty Research Institute) marked with the CC0 icon can be downloaded without fees.
practice_library.licence: CC0.
practice_library.notes: Includes prints, drawings and photographs.

practice_library.title: Wellcome Collection
practice_library.free_notes: Home page was reachable. Footer says site content is CC BY 4.0 except where noted, but it does not state image terms.
practice_library.licence: Per item; not confirmed.
practice_library.notes: Likely useful for historical anatomy plates; confirm the licence on each item page before using it.

practice_library.free_notes: Annual October ink challenge with an official daily prompt list. The site's robots rules blocked my fetch, so the current prompt list and any paid extras were not seen.
practice_library.licence: Not read.

practice_library.title: Exquisite corpse drawing game
practice_library.free_notes: Surrealist fold-over game: each person draws one body section (head, torso, legs, feet) without seeing the rest. Solo version: draw each section from a different random prompt.
practice_library.licence: Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA (standard footer, not seen in my fetch).
practice_library.notes: Good fuel for the 'draw random crazy things' session.

practice_library.free_notes: Free generator; pick how many words and a difficulty. Ads appear and there is a paid ad-removal option.

practice_library.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques
practice_library.provider: Dunlosky, Rawson, Marsh, Nathan, Willingham; Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 2013
practice_library.free_notes: The APS summary page is free. It links the full text on SAGE, and the page does not say whether that is open.
practice_library.licence: Publisher copyright.
practice_library.notes: Takeaway for drawing: space your sessions and test yourself (redraw from memory) instead of rereading or re-watching lessons; the review rated practice testing and spacing high and rereading low.

practice_library.title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention
practice_library.free_notes: Free PDF hosted by the authors' lab.
practice_library.licence: Publisher copyright; author-hosted copy.
practice_library.notes: Takeaway for drawing: close the lesson and draw its key idea from memory before you check, because recalling beat restudying on tests after a delay.

practice_library.title: Making Things Hard on Yourself, But in a Good Way
practice_library.provider: Bjork and Bjork, 2011 (UCLA Bjork Learning and Forgetting Lab)
practice_library.free_notes: Free PDF hosted by the lab.
practice_library.licence: Publisher copyright; lab-hosted copy.
practice_library.notes: Takeaway for drawing: mix subjects within a session (interleave) and space them out; it feels slower, but it carries over better than drilling one thing in a block.

practice_library.title: The Power of Feedback
practice_library.provider: Hattie and Timperley; Review of Educational Research, 2007
practice_library.free_notes: Abstract and tables are visible; the page marks the full text as restricted access.
practice_library.licence: Publisher copyright.
practice_library.notes: Takeaway for drawing: ask for feedback on the task and how to improve it, and compare against your last attempt; praise alone had the weakest effect in the tables shown.

practice_library.title: The Learning Scientists downloadable materials
practice_library.free_notes: Free posters, slides, bookmarks and strategy sheets on spaced practice, retrieval practice, elaboration, interleaving, concrete examples and dual coding.
practice_library.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: credit them, no commercial use, no changes.
practice_library.notes: Takeaway for drawing: a one-page poster of the six strategies is enough; do not turn it into a notebook project.

practice_library.licence: Publisher copyright.
practice_library.notes: Unverified link. Core idea: practice with a clear target, feedback and repetition at the edge of your ability.

weekly_templates.name: 3 hours a week: keep the thread
weekly_templates.description: Four short sessions on evenings and the weekend, which leaves Tuesday and Thursday free for jiu-jitsu. One lesson, one timed-reference session, one longer practice block, and one session of drawing whatever you like. If a session is missed, drop it rather than stacking it onto the next day.

sessions.focus: One lesson from the current module: 10 minutes watching or reading, 20 minutes on its exercise
Warm up with 30-second gestures, then 2-minute poses, then 3 minutes drawing the last lesson's key idea from memory with the lesson closed
Apply the week's lesson in one longer drawing from a photo bank or museum image, then 15 minutes comparing it to the source or posting for feedback
Draw random crazy things: roll two random words and a folklore creature, no erasing, no tutorials, no rules

weekly_templates.name: 6 hours a week: steady progress
weekly_templates.description: Two weeknight lessons, a short post-jiu-jitsu warm-up that is optional, a Friday accuracy session, and a long weekend block. Includes timed reference most weeks and a master copy from a museum open-access image. Sunday ends with a short check: draw last week's hardest idea from memory.

sessions.focus: Lesson (15 minutes) plus its exercise (30 minutes)
Timed reference: 10 minutes of gestures or quick poses, then 35 minutes on the module's exercise from reference
Optional after training, about 20:15: ellipses, boxes or line drills only. Skip if tired
Accuracy drawing from a photo using sighting, then overlay the photo to see where you drifted
60 minutes applying the module to a bigger drawing, 60 minutes copying a master drawing or painting from a museum open-access image

45 minutes of drawing random crazy things (random words, creature lists, exquisite corpse), then 30 minutes: blank-page recall of last week's lesson, pick the best piece and write two lines on what to fix

weekly_templates.name: 10 hours a week: push hard
weekly_templates.description: Daily sessions with two long weekend blocks. Weeknights are an hour on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, with only a light 30 minutes after jiu-jitsu on Tuesday and Thursday. Saturday is for structured long work; Sunday is half free play and half review. Cut this back to the 6-hour plan in any week work gets heavy.

sessions.focus: After jiu-jitsu, about 20:15: ten 1-minute gestures and 20 minutes of ellipses or box drills
Timed reference for 20 minutes (figure, hands or animals), then a 40-minute observed drawing
After jiu-jitsu: sketchbook page drawn from memory of something you saw today, then check against a photo
Second lesson application plus an overlay accuracy check on one drawing
Three one-hour blocks: master copy from a museum image, a construction or perspective project, and a long pose or portrait from reference
90 minutes of drawing random crazy things in any medium, 30 minutes of review and one critique request, 60 minutes trying a new medium or a digital tool on the week's best idea
